topIssues.title: op-challenger: support ZK dispute games in CLI commands
topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
Some op-challenger CLI commands do not yet support ZK games.

| Command | Status | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `list-games` | works | lists game type 10 |
| `move --attack` | works | attaches `challengerBond()` |
| `list-claims` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `list-credits` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `game-proposal-outputs` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `resolve` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `resolve-claim` | fails | `unsupported game type: zk` |
| `create-game` | builds an invalid tx | reverts `BadExtraData()` |
| `run-trace` | accepts `zk`, cannot run it | no executor for the type |

## Root cause

`list-claims`, `list-credits`, `game-proposal-outputs`, `resolve` and `resolve-claim` all construct via `NewFaultDisputeGameContract` (`faultdisputegame.go:84`), which has no ZK case. The generic `NewDisputeGameContract` (`disputegame.go:52`) does — that is why `move` works.

## In scope

**`resolve`** — switch `resolve.go:15` to `DisputeGameContract` / `NewDisputeGameContract`, as `move.go:90` does. `ResolveTx()` is already on that interface.

**`list-credits`** — `GetBalanceAndDelay` and `GetWithdrawals` are already on `ZKDisputeGameContract` (`zkdisputegame.go:79-81`). Only the recipient set differs: challenger, prover and game creator instead of the claim tree.

**`game-proposal-outputs`** — needs `--superroot-rpc` / `superroot_atTimestamp`, because `L2SequenceNum` is a super-root timestamp, not a block number. **Already broken for `super-cannon-kona` and `super-permissioned`** for the same reason: they construct fine, then feed a timestamp to `OutputAtBlock` (`game_proposal_outputs.go:174`, `superfaultdisputegame.go:63`). That file has no super-game test coverage. The logic exists in `game/zk/actor.go`'s `SuperRootProvider`.

**`create-game`** — needed by the `op-challenger-invalid-proposal` CronJob (`ethereum-optimism/k8s`, every 12h). `createGameParams` (`gamefactory.go:313`) has no ZK case; ZK `extraData` is a 4-byte `parentIndex` plus a `SuperRootProof` (`ZKDisputeGame.sol:189-205`). Reuse the existing `encodeSuperRootProof` and add `--parent-index` defaulting to `uint32.max`, which anchors to the `AnchorStateRegistry` root and keeps the cron invocation unchanged. Note `initBonds(10)` is non-zero (0.021 ETH on zk-proofs-1) and is forfeited on each invalid proposal.

**ZK game state** — nothing exposes `claimData()` (proposal status, challenger, prover, deadline), which is what confirms a proof landed after a challenge. Needs a ZK branch in `list-claims` or a new subcommand.

**`list-games`** (cosmetic) — prints `Claims 0`, because `GetClaimCount` is only called for `FaultDisputeGameContract` (`list_games.go:134`).

`credits.go`, `resolve.go`, `resolve_claim.go` and `create_game.go` have no test files; follow the stub-RPC pattern in `move_test.go`.

## Out of scope

**`resolve-claim`** — ZK games have no `resolveClaim`. Improve the error message only.

**`run-trace`** — ZK has no VM trace. The bug is that `--run zk/...` is accepted: `PlayableGameTypes` (`game_type.go:43`) backs the parser, but `serverExecutorForGameType` (`runner/factory.go:61`) has no case for it — same for `alphabet` and `fast`. Add a separate trace-types list; `PlayableGameTypes` must keep ZK, since it also backs `--game-type`, config validation and the monitor.

topIssues.title: kona-interop: the proof cost of message validation grows as executing messages × initiating-block receipts
topIssues.author: Inphi
topIssues.body:
## Summary

For each executing message, `MessageGraph` walks to the initiating block's header and decodes all of that block's receipts. Nothing is cached, and identical messages are not deduplicated. `CrossL2Inbox.validateMessage` costs about 3.5k gas after the first call, so one transaction can emit about 11k messages that all point to one log in a block with large receipts.

## Measurements

SP1 executor, real guest ELF:

| Receipts | Messages | Cycles |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | 1 | 7.0M |
| 512 | 64 | 443M |
| 2048 | 256 | 6.94B |

The rate is about 13k cycles for each (message × receipt). An attack with about 11k messages against about 1 MB of receipts is about 4e11 cycles for one timestamp. One timestamp cannot be split across consolidation proofs.

## Where

- `rust/kona/crates/protocol/interop/src/graph.rs:198-211`: one header walk and one receipts decode for each message.
- `rust/kona/crates/proof/proof-interop/src/provider.rs:106-132`: a full receipts decode, with no cache.

## Impact

Liveness in interop clusters. For a few dollars of L2 gas, an attacker can make the proof for one timestamp too expensive to finish in `maxProveDuration`. The attacker then challenges each honest game that covers that timestamp and takes the bonds. The FPVM uses the same algorithm, but it has no prove deadline.

## Fix

1. Cache headers by number and decoded receipts by block hash, across messages and across consolidation iterations.
2. Validate each distinct identifier once.
3. Index logs so that each lookup costs a fixed amount, not a full walk.

topIssues.title: kona/tests/proofs: run on op-reth-test-engine and delete op-e2e/e2eutils/gethengine
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #21905. Depends on #23343, #23344 and #21787.

Move the harness onto `op-reth-test-engine`, then delete the in-process op-geth L2 EL.

- [`env.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/rust/kona/tests/proofs/helpers/env.go#L82) builds the actions [`L2Engine`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/op-e2e/actions/helpers/l2_engine.go) instead of `gethengine.NewL2Engine`.
- Engine control:
  - Replace `EngineApi.IncludeTx` with `IncludeTxErr`.
  - Add `L2Engine.SetForceEmpty`, `ActL2IncludeTxIgnoreForcedEmpty` and `BlockByHash`.
- [`runner.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/rust/kona/tests/proofs/helpers/runner.go#L144) gives kona-host the engine socket path instead of `HTTPEndpoint()`.
- The pre-fork state generator ([`StateAt`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/rust/kona/tests/proofs/prefork_state_gen_test.go#L68), run by [`just nut-prefork-state-for`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/justfile#L484-L490)) reads state through `optest_dumpAccounts`.
- Delete [`op-e2e/e2eutils/gethengine`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/tree/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/op-e2e/e2eutils/gethengine).
- Build and CI:
  - [`action-tests-build`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/rust/kona/tests/justfile#L149-L153) and the generator recipe also build `op-reth-test-engine`.
  - [`kona-proof-action-tests`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/.circleci/continue/rust-e2e.yml#L159-L194) and [`kona-sp1-action-tests`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/.circleci/continue/rust-e2e.yml#L447-L470) export `RUST_BINARY_PATH_OP_RETH_TEST_ENGINE`. The binary is already in the workspace release builds they attach.
- Add a timeout on kona-host runs so that a witness gap fails the test instead of hanging it.
- Docs: [`fault-proofs.md`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/docs/ai/fault-proofs.md#L90-L113), [`opgeth-decoupling.md`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md#L721).

The PR for this closes #21905.

topIssues.title: op-reth-test-engine: serve the debug_ methods kona-host needs
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #21905. Stack on #21787's tip. This needs the [`OpEthApi` module](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/rust/op-reth-test-engine/src/rpc.rs#L154-L175) from #23198, and #21787 also edits that file.

Serve the `debug_` methods kona-host `super` calls on its L2 node. These are what production op-reth serves to kona-host: `eth_getProof`, `eth_getBlockBy*` and `eth_chainId` are served already, and IPC is enough (no HTTP listener).

- **`debug_getRawHeader`, `debug_getRawReceipts`, `debug_dbGet` (code form):** mount reth's [`DebugApi`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/blob/0fbe428518594611bdd3fdd822eb5968823c8e66/crates/rpc/rpc/src/debug.rs#L65-L70) over the existing `OpEthApi`. It needs a `reth_tasks::Runtime` on the current tokio handle.
- **`debug_executePayload`:** mount op-reth's [`OpDebugWitnessApi`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c3b34f1cf34e00d7cab7d1425e1e08783af52abf/rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/witness.rs#L81-L91) with an `OpPayloadBuilder` over a no-op pool, as the [production node does](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c3b34f1cf34e00d7cab7d1425e1e08783af52abf/rust/op-reth/crates/node/src/node.rs#L866-L912).
- **`optest_dumpAccounts(blockHash, addresses)`:** full account and storage state for the pre-fork state generator. reth's [`debug_dumpBlock`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/blob/0fbe428518594611bdd3fdd822eb5968823c8e66/crates/rpc/rpc/src/debug.rs#L1061-L1063) and [`debug_storageRangeAt`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/blob/0fbe428518594611bdd3fdd822eb5968823c8e66/crates/rpc/rpc/src/debug.rs#L1158-L1166) are stubs. Implement it by merging genesis plain state with the canonical in-memory blocks' bundle states, honoring storage wipes.
- **Socket-path accessor for kona-host:** `ipc.Proc.Path` → `testengine.Client.SocketPath` → `L2Engine.RPCEndpoint`. The [socket path is already owned by `Proc`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/5eaa2e6cb3fdfb6e0aa61043c8d2759e34c41579/op-service/ipc/ipc.go#L55-L64).
- **Tests:**
  - Raw header and receipts round-trip.
  - Witness check: `debug_executePayload` for a built block's parent and attributes returns the parent state-root node and the code of touched contracts.
  - Dump of a predeploy after a storage change.

Risks:
- **A witness gap hangs instead of failing.** reth's `debug_dbGet` serves [code only](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/blob/0fbe428518594611bdd3fdd822eb5968823c8e66/crates/rpc/rpc/src/debug.rs#L1037-L1058). So a node outside the witness is unservable, and kona-host [retries forever](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c3b34f1cf34e00d7cab7d1425e1e08783af52abf/rust/kona/bin/host/src/backend/online.rs#L143-L182). Production op-reth would hit the same gap.
- **Witness cost grows with chain length.** The witness is computed over the [in-memory overlay](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/reth/blob/0fbe428518594611bdd3fdd822eb5968823c8e66/crates/chain-state/src/memory_overlay.rs#L202-L210), which is the production path for unpersisted blocks. Each call merges every in-memory block, so a from-genesis proof sweep is quadratic in chain length. That is fine at action-test sizes.
- **A parent on a reorged-out fork is invisible to the provider.** Side chains live in the engine's tree state. The tests only prove the final canonical chain.

Size: S–M.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topIssues.title: kona/tests/proofs: read the L2 chain over RPC instead of the in-process chain
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #21905.

Replace the harness's in-process `core.BlockChain` reads (`env.Engine.L2Chain()…`) with eth RPC reads. They then work unchanged on today's in-process op-geth engine and on `op-reth-test-engine` after the cutover. Because the change is engine-agnostic, it can land on develop and is verified by the current `kona-proof-action-tests` job.

- `CurrentBlock`/`CurrentHeader`/`CurrentSafeBlock` → header by `latest`/`safe` label.
- `GetBlockByHash`/`GetBlockByNumber`/`GetHeaderBy*` → `ethclient`. Where geth returned nil, `ethclient` returns an error, so adjust the `NotNil` assertions.
- `GetReceiptsByHash` → `BlockReceipts`. op-reth's RPC receipts carry the Jovian [`daFootprintGasScalar` and `blobGasUsed`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c3b34f1cf34e00d7cab7d1425e1e08783af52abf/rust/op-reth/crates/rpc/src/eth/receipt.rs#L355-L364) that [`jovian_dafootprint_test.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c3b34f1cf34e00d7cab7d1425e1e08783af52abf/rust/kona/tests/proofs/jovian_dafootprint_test.go#L143-L154) reads.
- `L2Chain().Config()` → `env.Sd.L2Cfg.Config`, the genesis config the engine is built from.
- Delete dead code:
  - [`L2RPCTracker`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c3b34f1cf34e00d7cab7d1425e1e08783af52abf/rust/kona/tests/proofs/helpers/l2_rpc_tracker.go) and [`WithL2RPCTracker`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c3b34f1cf34e00d7cab7d1425e1e08783af52abf/rust/kona/tests/proofs/helpers/env.go#L171-L176). Nothing calls them, and the proxy only speaks HTTP.
  - The never-read [`FaultProofProgramL2Source.ChainConfig`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c3b34f1cf34e00d7cab7d1425e1e08783af52abf/rust/kona/tests/proofs/helpers/fixture.go#L19), set at [`runner.go`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/c3b34f1cf34e00d7cab7d1425e1e08783af52abf/rust/kona/tests/proofs/helpers/runner.go#L68).

Out of scope: engine control (`EngineApi.*`, force-empty), the kona-host endpoint and `StateAt`. Those move in the cutover.

Size: S–M, mechanical.

topPRs.title: Add Lean proof of the super-aggregation coverage checks
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Adds a Lean proof that `SuperAggregationInputs::validate` only accepts aggregations whose child outputs form one contiguous chain of super roots from the starting root to the root claim, with one range-derived block per chain and one consolidation step at every timestamp in between.

The Rust is extracted with Charon and Aeneas into `rust/kona/sp1/verification`. The main theorem is `KonaSp1.aggregation_sound`. It assumes child-proof soundness and `l2_sequence_number < u64::MAX`; the README lists the full trust base. `#print axioms` shows only Lean's standard axioms and the opaque super-root hash.

The `super_root.rs` change is only to suit the extractor: loops that returned early from nested or post-`?` positions move into private helpers, with the same accepted inputs and error order. A new test covers a chain-ID mismatch in a later timestamp block, the one loop that was rewritten rather than moved.

CI does not build the Lean project yet. `scripts/extract.sh` regenerates the generated files and `lake build` checks the proofs.

topPRs.title: op-chain-ops: add eth-liquidity-pause command
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23348 (`karl/eth-liquidity-pause`). That PR makes `ETHLiquidity` mirror the chain's L1 pause through the permissionless `L1CrossDomainMessenger.syncETHLiquidityPause()`.

## What it's for

`op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause` is a small CLI for the ETHLiquidity pause. It has three uses:

- **Devnet gate `interop.eth-liquidity-pause`:** `devnet-pause` → `status --expect paused` → `devnet-unpause` → `status --expect unpaused`.
- **Production verification:** `status` is read-only and works on any chain. Production pausing stays with the guardian's existing DeputyPauseModule flow, and this tool never pauses production. Nothing new is needed in superchain-ops.
- **Mirroring an L1 pause (or unpause, or expiry) to L2:** `sync` is permissionless, so any funded key can run it.

## Commands

- **`status --l2 <rpc>... [--l1 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr>...] [--expect paused|unpaused] [--json]`**
  - For each chain it reads `ETHLiquidity.paused()` and `pausedL1Timestamp()`.
  - It runs an `eth_call` of `SuperchainETHBridge.sendETH` with 1 wei. A state override funds the dummy `--from`, so the sender needs no balance. It reports whether the call reverts and with which error (selector and name).
  - With `--l1`, it also shows `L1CrossDomainMessenger.paused()`, which is the ETHLockbox pause, and prints `OUT OF SYNC` when L1 and L2 differ.
  - `--expect` exits non-zero on any mismatch. For `paused`, every chain needs `paused()` true, `sendETH` reverting with `ETHLiquidity_Paused()` and, if read, L1 paused.
- **`sync --l1 <rpc> --l2 <rpc> --l1-messenger <addr> ... --key <any funded key>`**
  - Checks that each messenger's `SystemConfig.l2ChainId()` matches the `--l2` it is paired with.
  - Prints the L1 and L2 state per chain and skips chains already in sync (`--force` overrides).
  - Calls `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, waits for the L1 receipt, then polls L2 until `paused()` equals the L1 pause at the sync's block, or `--timeout` passes.
- **`devnet-pause` / `devnet-unpause --guardian-key <key>`**
  - Resolves each chain's ETHLockbox identifier through messenger → SystemConfig → portal → lockbox. Chains that share a lockbox are handled once.
  - Checks that the key is the SuperchainConfig guardian.
  - Calls `pause`, `extend` (if an earlier pause expired) or `unpause` on the lockbox identifier, then runs `sync`.
  - `devnet-unpause` warns if a global pause is still active.
  - Refuses OP Mainnet, Ink, Unichain, their Sepolia chains (10, 57073, 130, 11155420, 763373, 1301) and an L1 of Ethereum mainnet. There is no override flag.

Every flag can also come from `--config <toml>` (see `config.example.toml`). Local `*.toml` files in that directory are gitignored because they may hold keys.

## Usage

```bash
# Production / any chain: read-only
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status \
  --l2 https://mainnet.optimism.io --l2 <ink-rpc> --l2 <unichain-rpc> \
  --l1 <eth-rpc> --l1-messenger <op-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <ink-l1cdm> --l1-messenger <uni-l1cdm>

# Mirror the current L1 pause to L2 (permissionless)
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause sync --config pause.toml --key <funded-l1-key>

# Devnet gate
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-pause   --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect paused
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause devnet-unpause --config devnet.toml
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause status         --config devnet.toml --expect unpaused
```

## Tests

None of these tests need a network.

- **Calldata:** encoding for `paused()`, `syncETHLiquidityPause()`, `sendETH`, and SuperchainConfig `pause`/`unpause`/`extend`/`pausable`/`paused(address)`.
- **ABI drift:** a test checks every hand-written signature and custom error against the contracts-bedrock ABI snapshots on this stack, so a rename in #23348 fails here.
- **Revert decoding:** custom errors and `Error(string)` reasons.
- **Safety checks:** production refusal, `--l2`/`--l1-messenger` pairing, grouping chains by shared lockbox, the guardian pause/extend/unpause choice, and `--expect` evaluation, including L1 paused while L2 is not synced.
- **Config loading:** TOML values load into each command, including the example config.
- **`status` end to end:** runs against in-process fake L1/L2 JSON-RPC servers. The cases are paused and synced, unpaused, out of sync, a pre-pause ETHLiquidity, a messenger paired with the wrong chain, and JSON output. The fake rejects `sendETH` without the balance override, as geth does.
- **`sync` end to end:** runs on geth simulated backends with mock contracts. The cases are skip when in sync, `--force` send and wait for L2, a reverting call never sent, and an L2 timeout.

```
go test ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # ok
go vet ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...    # clean
./linter/bin/op-golangci-lint run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/eth-liquidity-pause/...   # 0 issues
go mod tidy -diff                                    # clean
```

I also ran `status` read-only against OP Mainnet and OP Sepolia public RPCs. ETHLiquidity is not initialized there yet, and the tool reports `Error("Proxy: implementation not initialized")` for both reads.

**Not run:** `sync` and `devnet-*` against a live devnet with #23348 deployed. The guardian path (`devnet-pause`/`devnet-unpause`) has unit coverage only for its decision logic.

topPRs.title: op-reth: fix reth v2.6.0 review findings
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
This fixes the blocking findings from my review of #23046. Each one is a regression that the reth v2.6.0 bump introduces. Stacked on #23046.

- **Isthmus withdrawals root:** with state masking on (the new default), an op-reth sequencer could write a wrong `withdrawalsRoot` into a block header, and a verifier could reject a valid block with `L2WithdrawalsRootMismatch`. The cause is upstream: `OverlayStateProvider::storage_root` ignored the overlay trie nodes. The fix lives in ethereum-optimism/reth#11, and this PR pins reth to that commit. A regression test, masked and unmasked over both storage versions, fails on #23046.
- **`op-reth proofs init`:** init now refuses a datadir whose state trie lags its tip, or where reth's repair of it was interrupted, which happens after an unclean shutdown or on a snapshot of a running node. Before, init seeded a proofs store that matched no block. With backfill, that then failed with `StateRootMismatch`; without backfill, the node silently served wrong historical proofs. The error tells operators to start the node once and stop it cleanly.
- **Block access lists:** `debug_getRawBlockAccessList` is no longer served. op-reth now refuses to start with `--rpc-cache.prewarm-bals` or `--rpc-cache.cache-computed-bals`: on OP, prewarming re-executes every block forever, and it feeds the untested block access list reconstruction into tracing.
- **Flashblock log stream:** `flashblock_receipts_stream` returns logs for filters with an address or topic again. Since the bump, it returned none for them.

**Before merge:** keep this as a draft until ethereum-optimism/reth#11 merges, then re-pin to the merged commit. The current pin is reachable only from the fork PR's branch.

**Not addressed:**
- Low-impact test-helper refactors suggested by the Rust review: a shared `RethTrieStorageLayout` conversion, named test tuples, and a network-args helper.
- A pre-existing issue: flashblock stream logs carry per-flashblock, hash-ordered `transaction_index`/`log_index`.

🤖 *Co-created with Claude Opus 5.5*

topPRs.title: kona: avoid repeated interop message validation work
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Reduces interop proof cost when many executing messages reference the same source block by avoiding repeated header walks, receipt decoding, and log scans. Duplicate declarations are validated once after full cycle detection.

Historical source data is released between block groups; only current safe-head receipts persist across consolidation attempts. Log hashes are computed on demand, and replacement headers are reused from memory.

Locally verified with 103 native tests in the affected crates, isolated default-feature test builds, formatting, and scoped Clippy.
Guest cycles, from the SP1 executor running the `super-range` ELF on a consolidation step. One initiating block, all messages valid:

| Receipts × messages | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 64 × 1 | 7.1M | 7.2M |
| 512 × 64 | 450M | 16.9M |
| 2048 × 256, distinct identifiers | 7.07B | 50.0M |
| 2048 × 256, one identifier | 7.07B | 49.0M |

Cost now grows with messages plus receipts, not with their product. Each extra duplicate message costs about 11k cycles. VM memory and messages that point to many distinct source blocks have not been measured.

Fixes https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/23209
